items.snippet: Apple's wall-mounted HomeView will ship without a power adapter, USB-C cable, or mount, requiring customers to purchase compatible accessories separately. In a support document posted on October 14, Apple outlined different power requirements for the two versions of its new smart home hub. The tabletop HomeView requires a USB-C power adapter rated for at least 30W, supporting an output of 15V at 2A or higher. The wall-mounted model requires at least 20W, with support for 9V at 2.22A or higher. The tabletop model includes a 30W power adapter and a 1.5-meter USB-C cable. items.title: Rare Apple-1 With Steve Jobs Letter Sells for $1.15 Million
items.snippet: The "Hatfield" Apple-1 has sold for $1,148,200 including the buyer's premium, setting a world auction record for a commercially sold Apple-1, according to Bonhams . Two bidders competed for 28 minutes before the October 14 auction closed, taking the working computer beyond its $500,000 to $800,000 estimate . The machine takes its name from original owner Fred Hatfield, who complained to Apple about the lack of software for the Apple-1. A letter included in the sale contains Steve Jobs' 1978 reply, offering an Apple II motherboard in exchange for the Apple-1 and another $400 . Hatfield kept his computer. He eventually sold it privately for $40,000 while it needed repairs.

items.title: IDC: Apple closes in on Samsung as global smartphone shipments see record decline in Q3
items.snippet: In a report published today, IDC says Apple saw a 4% year-over-year decline in global iPhone shipments during Q3 2026, but its share of worldwide smartphone shipments increased 23.1% over the same period last year. Here’s why. IDC says its preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for Q3 2026 show a 22% drop compared to Q3 2025, which is in line with other regional and global trends reported recently. The culprit, as even occasional 9to5Mac readers are likely well aware by now, is the ongoing memory shortage, which has sent component costs soaring and squeezed device manufacturers, particularly those competing in lower-end markets. According to IDC, Samsung remained atop the ranking with 57.8 million units shipped and a 22.6% share, down 5.8% from the year-ago period. Apple came in second with 57.3 million shipped units, followed by Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo. The report shows OPPO seeing the biggest drop among the top five, with shipments down 34.5% year over year, and Apple recording the smallest decline at 4%. items.title: Today in Apple history: Former CEO John Sculley bids Apple a $10 million farewell
items.snippet: October 15, 1993: John Sculley, the former CEO responsible for forcing Steve Jobs out of Apple, is forced to leave the company himself. When Sculley resigns as Apple’s chairman, he leaves with a golden parachute. His parting gifts include $1 million in severance pay, a one-year consulting fee of $750,000, a commitment from Apple to buy his $4 million mansion and $2 million Learjet, and $2.4 million in stock options. Total take: around $10 million. John Sculley came to Apple to help Steve Jobs change the world. A decade later, he exited a company in crisis with a multimillion-dollar farewell package in tow. The former Pepsi-Cola Company executive famously helped push Jobs out in 1985, then presided over Apple’s rise into a multibillion-dollar business — and its slide toward the turmoil of the 1990s. Sculley resignation on this day in 1993 ended one of the most consequential and controversial chapters in Apple’s history. But his departure was more than the end of a CEO’s run. items.title: HomePod mini gets its biggest upgrade in 6 years
items.snippet: The HomePod mini 2, revealed Tuesday as part of Apple’s renewed push into the smart home, looks the same as its predecessor. However, the updated smart speaker comes in new colors and features upgraded internals for an enhanced Siri AI experience. “HomePod mini 2 brings together Siri AI, gorgeous new colors, and incredible audio,” said Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of worldwide home product marketing, in a press release. The new set-top box arrived alongside the HomeView smart hub and the Apple Home Collection of smart home accessories. Apple released the first HomePod mini in November 2020, so its successor arrives nearly six years later. From the outside, the speaker looks the same, but inside, it uses Apple’s S10 chip to deliver better dynamic range, loudness and acoustic performance. The only notable visual upgrade is the addition of sound glow at the top of the speaker. Apple describes it as a “visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble.” It even automatically picks up colors from the currently playing song’s art…

items.snippet: Macworld The touchscreen MacBook is reportedly going to be a reality very soon ( October 28 , apparently), and one of the questions about the new way to interface with the Mac is how macOS will accommodate our fingers. items.title: HomeView quickly won a place in my heart—and my home
items.snippet: Macworld Apple has taken its sweet time to make a smart display – just as it didn’t rush to make a folding phone. items.title: HomeView is right to break the rectangular mold
items.snippet: Macworld It can take a while to get used to the design of a completely new Apple product. Vision Pro, AirPods Max, even iPhone Duo all looked bizarre when they were first unveiled. So it shouldn’t be a surprise that right now, I feel like the HomeView looks weird. Possibly because it’s so square . Technically, of course, the screen of the HomeView is not a square but a squircle, because of the rounded corners. Everyone knows that the squircle was Steve Jobs’ favorite shape, which is why it crops up so much in Apple software design. items.title: iPhone 19 or iPhone 20? Apple’s 2027 anniversary iPhone rumors, specs and release date
items.snippet: Macworld The original iPhone was previewed in January 2007 and then released on June 29, 2007. So in 2027, it will turn 20 years old, and rumors point to Apple commemorating the event with a special 20th-anniversary model. It’s not expected to launch on June 29 (it will probably be in September, as usual), and it may not be a special one-off product, but rather the next major evolution of the iPhone, much like the iPhone X in 2017. But either way, the big two-oh is supposed to bring something really special. Will Apple call its next-generation models iPhone 19, or skip straight to iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary? The feature wasn’t exactly new—it had already been mentioned in a footnote on the iOS 27 page back in June — but there weren’t many details about how it would work until it arrived. items.title: New Home Collection banner offers Apple-influenced accessories
items.snippet: On Tuesday as a part of its deluge of smart home announcements, Apple has launched something a bit different: a series of products called Apple Home Collection that are… not quite Apple products, but not not Apple products. Instead, they’re “designed in collaboration” with partners, in this case LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. It’s hard to tell where one company ends and the other begins, but if you carry the weight of a brand like Apple, having Apple stand over the shoulder of some other company and sprinkle in some secret ingredients isn’t the worst approach if you don’t want to actually build and support those products yourself. According to Apple, each accessory can be set up with one tap from an iPhone, and only requires the Apple Home app. (That describes a lot of products today, too—it’ll be interesting to see if Apple’s added some new tech just for these products or if they’re largely using standard techniques that other products in the market can offer.) items.title: LPDDR5 5467 vs. 6400 vs. 7467 MT/s Memory Performance Benchmarks For Laptops
items.snippet: With the recently reviewed Star Labs StarFighter Ultra Linux laptop its BIOS allows for configurable memory speeds unlike many other laptop vendor BIOS implementations these days. Star Labs also made the default design decision to run the LPDDR5-7467 rated memory at LPDDR5-6400 speeds in the name of a balanced user experience for power/performance. So I was curious to run some benchmarks quantifying that power and performance impact of LPDDR5-6400 vs. LPDDR5-7467 plus tossed in LPDDR5-5467 testing as well as the third choice offered with this StarFighter Ultra laptop.

items.snippet: New market research from Counterpoint Research shows that global smartphone sales fell by 20% in the third quarter of this year compared with the same period a year ago.
